Animal Sudoku Rules

A small Sudoku for children: animals instead of numbers, and only 4 x 4 or 6 x 6 cells.

The rules

The board
The board has 4 x 4 cells in four boxes of 2 x 2, or 6 x 6 cells in six boxes of 2 rows and 3 columns. Thick lines show the boxes.
The animals
On 4 x 4 there are four animals: dog, cat, rabbit and mouse. On 6 x 6 the owl and the fish join them. Every animal appears exactly once in each row, each column and each box.
Given animals
Some animals are already on the board. They have a heavy frame and cannot be changed.
Playing
Choose an animal in the row of buttons under the board, then tap an empty cell. Tap it again with the same animal to take it off, or use the eraser. If an animal appears twice in a row, column or box, both get a dashed frame.
Hint
The Hint button works like Sudoku's: first it shows a mistake if there is one; otherwise it marks the next cell, then explains why, and on the third press puts the animal in.
Levels
Easy, Medium and Hard differ in how many animals are given at the start. Every puzzle has exactly one solution and can be solved without guessing.

A solved example

The picture shows a solved 4 x 4 board: in every row, every column and every 2 x 2 box, each of the four animals appears once.

Finishing a puzzle

Solved
The puzzle is solved when every cell holds the right animal.
